classification.habit: Large, glabrous, deciduous climbing shrub with succulent stems and aerial roots.
classification.habitat: Climbs over trees and hedges in forests, gardens and around habitations; often grown on Neem.
classification.distribution: Throughout tropical India, ascending to about 1,000 m.

identification.description: Large climbing shrub with succulent, corky-barked stems and thread-like aerial roots; cordate leaves, small greenish-yellow flowers and red pea-sized drupes.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial climber with corky warty stems, long thread-like aerial roots and heart-shaped leaves.
identification.root: Aerial roots long, filiform, hanging from the stem.
identification.stem: Pieces 0.6–5 cm thick; young stems green and smooth with swollen nodes; older stems light brown with warty lenticels; cut surface shows a radial wheel-like structure with conspicuous medullary rays; taste bitter.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, cordate, 5–10 cm long, membranous, long-petioled.
identification.flower: Small, greenish-yellow, unisexual, in axillary or terminal racemes, appearing when the plant is leafless.
identification.fruit: Drupes, ovoid, red when ripe, in clusters.
identification.bark: Thin, papery, creamy to grey-brown outer bark that peels off, with warty lenticels.
identification_points: Wheel-like radial pattern on cut stem
Warty lenticels on light brown papery bark

therapeutics.dose: Churna 3–6 g; kwatha 20–30 g drug; sattva 1–2 g
therapeutics.anupana: Ghee in Vata, sugar in Pitta, honey in Kapha, castor oil in Vatarakta and shunthi in Amavata (classical anupana of Guduchi).
therapeutics.precautions: May lower blood glucose; monitor with antidiabetic drugs. Use with care with immunosuppressants and in autoimmune disease. Use authenticated Tinospora cordifolia stem.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy and lactation without advice; avoid in severe constipation.

shlokas:
गुडूची कटुका तिक्ता स्वादुपाका रसायनी ।
संग्राहिणी कषायोष्णा लघ्वी बल्याऽग्निदीपनी ।
दोषत्रयामतृड्दाहमेहकासांश्च पाण्डुताम् ॥
कामलाकुष्ठवातास्रज्वरकृमिवमीन् हरेत् ।
प्रमेहश्वासकासार्शःकृच्छ्रहृद्रोगवातनुत् ॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Guduchyadi Varga, verses 8–9 in the searchable recension; edition numbering may vary.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The stem contains clerodane diterpenoids (tinosporaside, columbin), protoberberine and aporphine alkaloids (berberine, palmatine, magnoflorine) and glycosides.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Divine herb for immunity, detox and chronic fevers.
recognized_uses: Jwara, including Jirna and Vishama Jwara
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated; isolated reports of liver injury exist, often linked to misidentified species or concentrated products. Monitor glucose in diabetics.
